flask_admin/contrib/mongoengine/view.py:520:        # TODO: Unfortunately, MongoEngine contains bug which
flask_admin/contrib/mongoengine/view.py:521:        # prevents running complex Q queries and, as a result,
flask_admin/contrib/mongoengine/view.py:522:        # Flask-Admin does not support per-word searching like
flask_admin/contrib/mongoengine/view.py:523:        # in other backends
flask_admin/contrib/mongoengine/view.py:524:        op, term = parse_like_term(search_term)
flask_admin/contrib/mongoengine/view.py:525:
flask_admin/contrib/mongoengine/view.py:526:        criteria = None
flask_admin/contrib/mongoengine/view.py:527:
flask_admin/contrib/mongoengine/view.py:528:        for field in self._search_fields:
flask_admin/contrib/mongoengine/view.py:529:            if type(field) == mongoengine.ReferenceField:
flask_admin/contrib/mongoengine/view.py:530:                regex: str | re.Pattern[str] = re.compile(".*{term}.*")
flask_admin/contrib/mongoengine/view.py:531:            else:
flask_admin/contrib/mongoengine/view.py:532:                regex = term
flask_admin/contrib/mongoengine/view.py:533:            flt = {f"{field.name}__{op}": regex}
flask_admin/contrib/mongoengine/view.py:534:            q = mongoengine.Q(**flt)
flask_admin/contrib/mongoengine/view.py:535:
flask_admin/contrib/mongoengine/view.py:536:            if criteria is None:

flask_admin/contrib/mongoengine/view.py:538:            else:
flask_admin/contrib/mongoengine/view.py:539:                criteria |= q
flask_admin/contrib/mongoengine/view.py:540:
flask_admin/contrib/mongoengine/view.py:541:        return query.filter(criteria)

flask_admin/contrib/sqla/tools.py:98:def tuple_operator_in(

flask_admin/contrib/sqla/tools.py:100:) -> t.Any:
flask_admin/contrib/sqla/tools.py:101:    """The tuple_ Operator only works on certain engines like MySQL or Postgresql. It
flask_admin/contrib/sqla/tools.py:102:    does not work with sqlite.
flask_admin/contrib/sqla/tools.py:103:
flask_admin/contrib/sqla/tools.py:104:    The function returns an or_ - operator, that containes and_ - operators for every
flask_admin/contrib/sqla/tools.py:105:    single tuple in ids.
flask_admin/contrib/sqla/tools.py:106:
flask_admin/contrib/sqla/tools.py:107:    Example::
flask_admin/contrib/sqla/tools.py:108:
flask_admin/contrib/sqla/tools.py:109:      model_pk =  [ColumnA, ColumnB]
flask_admin/contrib/sqla/tools.py:110:      ids = ((1,2), (1,3))
flask_admin/contrib/sqla/tools.py:111:
flask_admin/contrib/sqla/tools.py:112:      tuple_operator(model_pk, ids)
flask_admin/contrib/sqla/tools.py:113:      ->
flask_admin/contrib/sqla/tools.py:114:      or_( and_( ColumnA == 1, ColumnB == 2), and_( ColumnA == 1, ColumnB == 3) )
flask_admin/contrib/sqla/tools.py:115:
flask_admin/contrib/sqla/tools.py:116:    The returning operator can be used within a filter(), as it is just an or_ operator
flask_admin/contrib/sqla/tools.py:117:    """
flask_admin/contrib/sqla/tools.py:118:    ands: list[t.Any] = []
flask_admin/contrib/sqla/tools.py:119:    for id in ids:
flask_admin/contrib/sqla/tools.py:120:        k = []
flask_admin/contrib/sqla/tools.py:121:        for i in range(len(model_pk)):
flask_admin/contrib/sqla/tools.py:122:            k.append(eq(model_pk[i], id[i]))
flask_admin/contrib/sqla/tools.py:123:        ands.append(and_(*k))
flask_admin/contrib/sqla/tools.py:124:    if len(ands) >= 1:
flask_admin/contrib/sqla/tools.py:125:        return or_(*ands)
flask_admin/contrib/sqla/tools.py:126:    else:
flask_admin/contrib/sqla/tools.py:127:        return None
